title: OAI family 127: Average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions
open: Does the average-sensitivity bound for polynomial threshold functions hold in full generality, and can the claimed proof of the degree-at-most-$d$ case be independently verified and formalized? In particular, the remaining scope of the Gotsman–Linial conjecture beyond what the claimed result covers is still open.
status: A manuscript (dated September 25, 2026) proves that a degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial threshold function on the uniform $n$-dimensional Boolean cube has average sensitivity at most $8d\sqrt{n}$, uniformly for $1\le d\le n$, where average sensitivity counts expected output changes under single-bit flips; this establishes the asymptotic Gotsman–Linial conjecture, allowing polynomial zeros with $\operatorname{sign}(0)=1$ ([Lean](lean/docs/127.md); [Average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions](preprints/Average-Sensitivity-of-Polynomial-Threshold-Functions-September-25-2026/main.pdf); repo: github.com/openai/math, family 127). Verification status varies; the result should be treated as a model-produced claim pending community review.
solved_when: A community-verified (and ideally formalized) proof that every degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial threshold function on the uniform $n$-dimensional Boolean cube has average sensitivity at most $8d\sqrt{n}$, uniformly for $1\le d\le n$, allowing polynomial zeros with $\operatorname{sign}(0)=1$, together with resolution of any remaining generality of the original conjecture not implied by this bound.
why: This is a frontier-model attack on an open research problem, so whether its verification and formalization hold up matters in its own right; a confirmed proof settles the asymptotic Gotsman–Linial conjecture, while a failure would leave the conjecture's remaining scope open.
key_works: [Average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions](preprints/Average-Sensitivity-of-Polynomial-Threshold-Functions-September-25-2026/main.pdf); repo: github.com/openai/math (family 127)
aliases: openai-math family 127; Average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions

title: OAI family 212: Planar first-passage geometry and the absence of bigeodesics

title: OAI family 354: The isoperimetric profile of the cubic three-torus

solved_when: The claim is independently verified (checked and, ideally, formalized) that the isoperimetric profile of the unit cubic flat three-torus is as stated, with minimizers classified as balls, circular tubes around shortest closed geodesics, coordinate slabs, and their complements, transition volumes $4\pi/81$ and $1/\pi$, and exactly the adjacent two types minimizing at each transition; and the remaining scope of the original problem is resolved.
why: This is a frontier-model attack on an open research problem, so its verification and formalization status is itself at stake for the field — a confirmed result settles the isoperimetric problem for this manifold, while a failure calibrates how far machine-produced proofs can be trusted.

title: OAI family 014: Restricted geometric Langlands, global Arthur enhancements, and generic Ramanujan
open: To what extent can the restricted geometric Langlands equivalence for connected reductive groups on smooth projective connected curves be extended beyond its currently claimed setting — over arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 0, and in full generality without the stated Lie-theoretic characteristic hypotheses? More broadly, which parts of the claimed framework (restricted geometric Langlands, global Arthur enhancements, and generic Ramanujan) survive independent verification, formalization, and removal of auxiliary assumptions such as the finite-level Ramanujan–Arthur decomposition?
status: Model-produced manuscripts claim: the restricted geometric Langlands equivalence for connected reductive groups on smooth projective connected curves over $\overline{\mathbb F}_q$ under four stated Lie-theoretic characteristic hypotheses; the same conclusion over arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 0 assuming additionally that p is very good for the group and $p \nmid |W_G|$; Ramanujan at every place for globally generic cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple exceptional groups over global function fields, without characteristic or ramification-depth restrictions; Ramanujan at every unramified place for cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple groups with a generic unramified component; and, assuming the finite-level Ramanujan–Arthur decomposition, construction of global Arthur enhancements of occurring cuspidal excursion parameters for split connected semisimple groups at full finite level, recovering the given parameters by diagonal specialization on the entire Weil group, including inertia. Manuscript dates: October 5, 2026, September 24, 2026. Verification status varies; the claims should be treated as pending community review. Key works: [Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters](preprints/Global-Arthur-Enhancements-of-Cuspidal-Excursion-Parameters-October-5-2026/manuscript.pdf); [Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration](preprints/Rationality-of-the-Canonical-Unramified-Arthur-Filtration-September-24-2026/paper.pdf); [Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level](preprints/Ramanujan-Arthur-Decompositions-of-Cuspidal-Functions-at-Full-Finite-Level-September-24-2026/paper.pdf); [Temperedness at ramified places for globally generic exceptional groups](preprints/Temperedness-at-ramified-places-for-globally-generic-exceptional-groups-October-5-2026/ramified-ramanujan.pdf); repo: github.com/openai/math (family 014).
solved_when: The restricted geometric Langlands equivalence holds for connected reductive groups on smooth projective connected curves over any algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0 (under the four Lie-theoretic characteristic hypotheses, or with the additional assumptions that p is very good for the group and p ∤ |W_G|); Ramanujan at every place holds for globally generic cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple groups (including exceptional ones), and at every unramified place for cuspidal representations with a generic unramified component; global Arthur enhancements of cuspidal excursion parameters are constructed at full finite level without assuming the finite-level Ramanujan–Arthur decomposition, recovering the given parameters by diagonal specialization on the entire Weil group including inertia — all verified by community review rather than resting on model-produced claims.
why: These claims constitute a frontier-model attack on a major open problem in the geometric Langlands program, so their verification and formalization status is itself of consequence for the field; a confirmed proof would extend restricted geometric Langlands, generic Ramanujan, and Arthur-type enhancement constructions well beyond previously known settings.

title: OAI family 015: Torus-packet equidistribution in prime, quartic, and sextic degrees

status: The manuscripts claim Haar equidistribution without escape of mass for complete volume-weighted torus packets from totally real fields: arbitrary lattices and prescribed local types in fixed prime degree at least five, arbitrary-order Picard packets in primitive quartic fields, and maximal-order ideal-class packets in primitive sextic fields, where primitive means having no proper intermediate field and the relevant order or field discriminant tends to infinity ([Lean](lean/docs/015.md)). Manuscript dates: October 5, 2026 and September 24, 2026. Verification status varies; treat as model-produced claims pending community review.
solved_when: The equidistribution claims are independently verified and, ideally, formalized; the results extend to the remaining scope beyond the stated cases (arbitrary lattices and prescribed local types in fixed prime degree at least five, arbitrary-order Picard packets in primitive quartic fields, and maximal-order ideal-class packets in primitive sextic fields, with primitive meaning no proper intermediate field and order or field discriminant tending to infinity).
why: These are frontier-model attacks on open research problems, so the correctness of the proofs — and the state of their verification and formalization — is itself at stake for the field; genuine proofs would settle equidistribution questions for broad classes of torus packets from totally real fields.

title: OAI family 017: The irrationality exponent of π is 2
open: Is the claimed proof that the irrationality exponent of π equals 2 correct, complete, and fully formalized? Beyond verifying this manuscript, the general question remains of rigorously establishing — and formally verifying — the exact irrationality exponent of π.
status: A manuscript (dated September 24, 2026) proves that the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2, i.e., that for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large denominators q, every rational p/q satisfies |π − p/q| ≥ q^{−2−ε}, and thereby also proves convergence of the Flint–Hills series ∑_{n≥1} 1/(n³ sin² n) with angles in radians ([The irrationality exponent of pi is 2](preprints/The-irrationality-exponent-of-pi-is-2-September-24-2026/paper.pdf); Lean documentation at [lean/docs/017.md](lean/docs/017.md); repo: github.com/openai/math, family 017). Verification status varies; the result should be treated as a model-produced claim pending community review.
solved_when: The claim that the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2 — i.e., that for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large denominators q, every rational p/q satisfies |π − p/q| ≥ q^{−2−ε} — is established by a proof that passes community review and is formalized, including the implied convergence of the Flint–Hills series ∑_{n≥1} 1/(n³ sin² n) with angles in radians.
why: The irrationality exponent of π is a basic unknown about one of mathematics' central constants, and the claimed result settles the Flint–Hills series convergence; moreover, this is a frontier-model attack on an open problem, so its verification and formalization status matters for the field.
key_works: [The irrationality exponent of pi is 2](preprints/The-irrationality-exponent-of-pi-is-2-September-24-2026/paper.pdf); repo: github.com/openai/math (family 017)

status: The manuscript "Primitive roots for every admissible integer base" (October 4, 2026) claims the infinitude assertion in Artin's primitive root conjecture for every integer a that is neither −1 nor a square, showing that for each such base at least $c_a x/(\log x)^2$ primes in every sufficiently large interval $(x,2x)$ have primitive root a, with $c_a > 0$. solved_when: The October 4, 2026 claim is independently verified (or formalized), and Artino's primitive root conjecture is established unconditionally for every integer a that is neither −1 nor a square — namely, that for each such base there are at least $c_a x/(\log x)^2$ primes with primitive root a in every sufficiently large interval $(x,2x)$, with $c_a > 0$.
why: The manuscript is a frontier-model attack on a classical open problem; whether its claimed proof of Artin's conjecture for all admissible bases survives verification directly determines the state of one of number theory's long-standing conjectures, and its formalization status matters for the field.

title: OAI family 034: Log abundance for compact Kähler spaces under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity

status: Using logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity, the manuscripts prove log abundance in every dimension for normal compact Kähler log canonical pairs with effective rational boundary: an analytically nef ℚ-Cartier adjoint is semiample. They also prove projective log abundance over every algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture for smooth projective varieties of nonnegative Kodaira dimension in that setting. A further result resolves the finite-rational-coefficient index conjecture for connected projective semi-log-canonical log Calabi–Yau pairs over such fields in each fixed dimension and for each fixed finite set of rational boundary coefficients, with a uniform index independent of the number of components. solved_when: The claimed manuscripts are verified by community review (log abundance in every dimension for normal compact Kähler log canonical pairs with effective rational boundary, where an analytically nef ℚ-Cartier adjoint is semiample; projective log abundance over every algebraically closed field of characteristic zero; the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture for smooth projective varieties of nonnegative Kodaira dimension; and the finite-rational-coefficient index conjecture for connected projective semi-log-canonical log Calabi–Yau pairs in each fixed dimension and fixed finite set of rational boundary coefficients, with a uniform index independent of the number of components), and the remaining scope of the original open problem is closed.

status: A manuscript dated September 24, 2026 ("P=W in composite rank for fixed determinant", preprint; repo: github.com/openai/math, family 043) proves P_k = W_{2k} = W_{2k+1} on the full rational cohomology of smooth coprime fixed-determinant, trace-free Higgs moduli spaces and their character varieties for composite ranks over smooth projective complex curves of genus at least two, including variant cohomology. Combined with the known prime-rank theorems, this claims the fixed-determinant P = W conjecture in every coprime rank. Verification status varies; the claim should be treated as model-produced pending community review.
solved_when: The fixed-determinant P = W conjecture is rigorously established in every coprime rank over smooth projective complex curves of genus at least two — i.e., the claim P_k = W_{2k} = W_{2k+1} on full rational cohomology (including variant cohomology) of the smooth coprime fixed-determinant, trace-free Higgs moduli spaces and their character varieties, for composite ranks, is verified and accepted alongside the known prime-rank theorems.
why: A verified proof closes the fixed-determinant P = W conjecture in all coprime ranks, connecting Hodge-theoretic and non-abelian Hodge structures on these moduli spaces; and because the current manuscript is a model-produced claim, its verification (or failure) also bears directly on how the field treats machine-generated proofs.

status: The claimed result resolves Schramm's Hausdorff-measure question for chordal SLEκ, $0\lt \kappa\lt 8$: the explicit gauge $r^d(\log\log(1/r))^{(2-d)/2}$, $d=1+\kappa/8$, gives almost surely positive finite measure to every trace segment $\gamma([s,t])$ with $0\lt s\lt t\lt \infty$, and finite expected measure to the trace in every bounded disk. title: OAI family 231: The free uniform spanning forest is a factor of IID
open: Is the claimed result — that the free uniform spanning forest on every infinite connected locally finite simple unweighted graph is a factor of IID — correct and complete in full generality? status: The manuscript (dated September 25, 2026) claims that on every infinite connected locally finite simple unweighted graph, the free uniform spanning forest is a factor of independent vertex labels, by one isomorphism-equivariant rule using no root, and that translation-invariant strongly Rayleigh binary processes on every countable group — including invariant determinantal processes with Hermitian positive-contraction kernels — are also factors of IID ([Lean](lean/docs/231.md)). solved_when: The claim is verified in full generality by community review and/or formalized: an isomorphism-equivariant, root-free factor of independent vertex labels producing the free uniform spanning forest on every infinite connected locally finite simple unweighted graph (and, as stated, translation-invariant strongly Rayleigh binary processes on every countable group, including invariant determinantal processes with Hermitian positive-contraction kernels, as factors of IID), with no unverified or unformalized parts remaining.
why: This is a frontier-model attack on an open research problem, so the correctness and formalization status of the claim itself matters for the field; a confirmed proof would establish the free uniform spanning forest as a factor of IID in this generality, while an unverified claim leaves the result unusable.

title: OAI family 232: Gaussian fields and interfaces for triangular-lattice Lipschitz heights
open: Do the Gaussian-field and interface predictions of Schramm for triangular-lattice Lipschitz height models hold in full generality, and are the claimed proofs for the two-arc boundary and weighted-height cases correct as stated? A complete answer would both verify the model-produced manuscripts under community review and extend the results beyond bounded smooth simply connected domains and the specific boundary conditions, increments $0,\pm2$, and weight range $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$ treated so far.
status: Manuscripts dated September 25, 2026 prove Gaussian free field limits on bounded smooth simply connected domains for triangular-lattice height models: uniform odd heights with increments $0,\pm2$ and two-arc boundary values $\pm1$, and zero-boundary integer Lipschitz heights weighted by fixed $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$. Uniform real Lipschitz heights also converge to a Gaussian field, and at a tuned opposite-boundary amplitude their interface converges to chordal SLE4, establishing Schramm's real-field/interface predictions. Verification status varies across the works; they should be treated as model-produced claims pending community review.
solved_when: The claimed convergence results are rigorously verified and extended to the remaining scope — full generality of domains, boundary conditions, and height models beyond uniform odd heights with increments $0,\pm2$ with two-arc boundary values $\pm1$ and zero-boundary integer Lipschitz heights weighted by $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$ — including the convergence of uniform real Lipschitz heights to a Gaussian field and, at the tuned opposite-boundary amplitude, of the interface to chordal SLE4.
why: These results establish Schramm's predictions that Gaussian free field limits and chordal SLE4 interfaces emerge from Lipschitz height models on the triangular lattice; moreover, because the manuscripts are model-produced and only partially verified, their confirmation or refutation directly informs how the field can rely on AI-generated proofs.

title: OAI family 235: Limiting random SAT thresholds, sharp variance and computability
open: Does a finite positive satisfiability threshold exist for random k-SAT in full generality, and can the remaining claims around it — sharp hitting-time variance and computability of threshold constants — be independently verified and fully formalized? status: For random k-SAT with independent uniformly signed proper clauses sampled with replacement, the family proves finite positive limiting thresholds and hitting-time variance $\Theta_k(n)$ for every fixed k ≥ 3, and computability of the 3-SAT threshold. title: OAI family 242: Single-fold Diophantine representations and undecidability under an at-most-one-solution promise

title: OAI family 244: The Partition Principle does not imply Choice
open: Does the Partition Principle — that every surjective image of a set injects back into that set — fail to imply the axiom of choice in full generality, and does the claimed model construction withstand independent verification? status: Assuming ZF is consistent, the claim constructs a model in which every surjective image of a set injects into that set, yet the axiom of choice fails, while choice for ordinal-indexed families still holds. solved_when: The claimed result is independently verified and community-reviewed (including formalization of the currently unformalized parts), and the residual open scope of the original Partition Principle versus Choice problem is resolved in full generality.
why: This is a frontier-model attack on a long-standing open problem in set theory, and its verification and formalization status itself matters for the field.

title: OAI family 251: Amenability, unitarizability, and strong Ulam stability

status: A model-produced manuscript (September 27, 2026; [preprint](preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), [Lean documentation](lean/docs/272.md), repo github.com/openai/math family 272) constructs an entangled state on $\mathbb C^{10}\otimes\mathbb C^{10}$ with zero distillable secret key for specified local-instrument protocols completing almost surely, allowing joint local processing and authenticated two-way public communication, with no other shared private resource and an eavesdropper holding the input purification and public record. It further gives a trace-preserving PPT channel on $M_{21}(\mathbb C)$ whose square is not entanglement breaking, disproving Christandl's PPT-square conjecture. Verification status varies; the claims should be treated as pending community review.
solved_when: The claim that an entangled state on $\mathbb C^{10}\otimes\mathbb C^{10}$ has zero distillable secret key under the specified protocols is rigorously verified (including the PPT channel on $M_{21}(\mathbb C)$ whose square is not entanglement breaking, refuting Christandl's PPT-square conjecture), and the question is settled for general protocols allowing joint local processing and authenticated two-way public communication with an eavesdropper holding the input purification and public record.
why: The construction refutes a standing conjecture about PPT channels and would establish the first entangled state in local dimension ten carrying no distillable secret key; because the manuscript is a model-produced claim pending community review, its verification status matters directly to the field.
key_works: [Entanglement with zero distillable secret key in local dimension ten](preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/paper.pdf); repo: github.com/openai/math (family 272)

title: OAI family 273: The entropy photon-number inequality
open: Does the entropy photon-number inequality hold in full generality, and is the claimed proof correct and complete? Beyond verifying the model-produced result for beam-splitter mixing of two independent finite-energy bosonic inputs, the remaining scope of the original problem — settings and formulations not covered by that claim, including any unformalized parts — is still open.
status: The record claims a proof of the entropy photon-number inequality for beam-splitter mixing of two independent finite-energy bosonic inputs in any finite number of modes: the output's entropy photon number is at least the transmissivity-weighted average of the inputs'. Arbitrary entanglement within each input is allowed, and product thermal inputs attain equality even when their entropies differ. solved_when: The entropy photon-number inequality for beam-splitter mixing of two independent finite-energy bosonic inputs in any finite number of modes is rigorously verified (including formalization or community review of the Lean proof), and the inequality is settled in the full generality of the original problem.

title: OAI family 274: Parity is not in QAC0
open: Beyond the announced manuscript, does parity genuinely fail to be computable by QAC0 in full generality — and can that claim be verified and formalized to the community's standard? The remaining scope is to confirm the claimed lower bound in its unrestricted form and complete the parts left unformalized.
status: A manuscript dated September 24, 2026 resolves Moore's parity conjecture in the measured-output model: constant-depth quantum circuits with arbitrary one-qubit gates, unbounded-arity Toffoli gates, and polynomially many total qubits cannot compute parity with any fixed positive worst-case advantage, where ancillas start in zero, one output qubit is measured, and all other registers may be discarded. Xu–Li's reductions give the same bounded-error obstruction for strict majority. Partial Lean documentation exists (lean/docs/274.md). Verification status varies; the result should be treated as a model-produced claim pending community review. Key works: [Product-projection localization and the QAC0 parity lower bound](preprints/Product-projection-localization-and-the-QAC0-parity-lower-bound-September-24-2026/paper.pdf); [Regular trajectories, pruning and quantum parity](preprints/Regular-trajectories-pruning-and-quantum-parity-September-24-2026/paper.pdf); repo: github.com/openai/math (family 274).
solved_when: The claim is verified by community review and fully formalized (the existing Lean documentation is extended to cover the full result), establishing that constant-depth quantum circuits with arbitrary one-qubit gates, unbounded-arity Toffoli gates, and polynomially many total qubits, with ancillas starting in zero, one output qubit measured, and all other registers discarded, cannot compute parity with any fixed positive worst-case advantage — and, via Xu–Li's reductions, the same bounded-error obstruction for strict majority.
why: A model-produced attack on an open problem means the verification and formalization status is itself at stake; settling it either delivers a genuine parity lower bound for QAC0 or exposes a gap that the field must still close.
key_works: [Product-projection localization and the QAC0 parity lower bound](preprints/Product-projection-localization-and-the-QAC0-parity-lower-bound-September-24-2026/paper.pdf); [Regular trajectories, pruning and quantum parity](preprints/Regular-trajectories-pruning-and-quantum-parity-September-24-2026/paper.pdf); repo: github.com/openai/math (family 274)

title: OAI family 277: Threshold repetition for entangled games
open: Does threshold parallel repetition truly hold in full generality for all finite two-player one-round entangled games? A claimed proof gives exponential decay of the probability of winning at least a $v+\delta$ fraction of $k$ repetitions whenever the entangled value is $v < 1$, but this is a model-produced manuscript whose full generality, correctness, and unformalized portions remain to be verified and established.
status: A manuscript dated September 25, 2026 proves exponential threshold repetition for every finite two-player one-round game: if its entangled value is $v < 1$, the probability of winning at least a fraction $v+\delta$ of $k$ independent repetitions decays exponentially in $k$, for $0 < \delta < 1-v$. Arbitrary joint finite-dimensional entangled strategies and correlated question distributions are allowed. A Lean document exists (lean/docs/277.md). Verification status varies; the result should be treated as a model-produced claim pending community review. ([Lean](lean/docs/277.md))

why: Verifying this frontier-model attack on an open problem would establish exponential threshold repetition for entangled games in full generality, and the verification and formalization status of such machine-produced proofs is itself at stake for how the field treats them.

title: OAI family 278: Failure of Kohn–Sham ensemble representation
open: Does there exist a Coulomb system whose exact ground-state density admits no Kohn–Sham representation at all — and, more immediately, does the claimed three-electron counterexample to ensemble representability hold up under independent verification and extend beyond its restricted setting?
status: The manuscript constructs a three-electron Coulomb molecule with two equal positive-integer-charge nuclei whose absolute ground-state density has no noninteracting ground-state ensemble representation by a single real spin-independent local potential in $`L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^3)+L^\infty(\mathbb R^3)`$, thereby disproving Kohn–Sham ensemble representability for that potential class; the required nuclear charge is specified nonnumerically. The manuscript is dated September 25, 2026, and its verification status varies; it should be treated as a model-produced claim pending community review. Reference: [A Coulomb ground-state density without Kohn-Sham ensemble representation](preprints/A-Coulomb-Ground-State-Density-without-Kohn-Sham-Ensemble-Representation-September-25-2026/paper.pdf); repo: github.com/openai/math (family 278).
solved_when: The manuscript's claim is independently verified (or refuted) by community review, and the representability question is settled in full generality — namely, whether the absolute ground-state density of the constructed three-electron Coulomb molecule with two equal positive-integer-charge nuclei truly lacks any noninteracting ground-state ensemble representation by a single real spin-independent local potential in $`L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^3)+L^\infty(\mathbb R^3)`$, and whether the counterexample extends to broader potential classes and numerically specified nuclear charges.
why: A verified counterexample would show that the Kohn–Sham construction — the foundation of practical density functional theory — can genuinely fail for real Coulomb systems, forcing a reassessment of when density-potential mappings exist. Moreover, since this is a frontier-model-produced claim, its verification or failure is itself informative about the reliability of AI attacks on open research problems.

title: OAI family 285: Counterexamples to Baum–Connes and Kadison–Kaplansky

solved_when: The manuscripts' claims are independently verified or refuted by community review, including the finitely generated torsion-free witness to the injectivity failure, the torsion-free group with a nontrivial projection in its reduced group C∗-algebra, and the irrational-trace counterexample; and the remaining scope of the original conjectures is settled.
why: Genuine counterexamples would overturn the coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes conjecture and the Kadison–Kaplansky conjecture for torsion-free groups, reshaping large parts of operator K-theory; moreover, these are model-produced claims whose verification status directly tests the reliability of AI-generated mathematics.

title: OAI family 335: Gromov’s integral scalar-curvature bound for simplicial volume
open: Can Gromov's hoped-for integral bound — that the negative part of scalar curvature controls the real simplicial volume from below — be established and verified in full generality, together with the claimed consequences for positive scalar curvature? In particular, is the claimed bound $\int_M(\mathrm{Scal}_g^-)^{n/2}\,dV_g\ge a_n\lVert M\rVert$ for all closed connected oriented smooth n-manifolds with n ≥ 3 and all smooth metrics, with $a_n\gt 0$ depending only on n, correct, and does rational inessentiality under positive scalar curvature hold?
status: Manuscripts claim the bound $\int_M(\mathrm{Scal}_g^-)^{n/2}\,dV_g\ge a_n\lVert M\rVert$ for every closed connected oriented smooth n-manifold, n ≥ 3, and every smooth metric, with $a_n\gt 0$ depending only on dimension, where $\mathrm{Scal}_g^-=\max\{0,-\mathrm{Scal}_g\}$ and $\lVert M\rVert$ is real simplicial volume; they also claim rational inessentiality under positive scalar curvature, resolving the Gromov–Lawson conjecture, and that every nonnegative-scalar-curvature metric on a closed aspherical manifold is flat. Manuscript dates: October 5, 2026, September 23, 2026. Verification status varies; treat as model-produced claims pending community review. Key works: [An integral scalar curvature bound for real simplicial volume](preprints/An-integral-scalar-curvature-bound-for-real-simplicial-volume-October-5-2026/v126-proof.pdf); [Positive scalar curvature forces rational inessentiality](preprints/Positive-scalar-curvature-forces-rational-inessentiality-September-23-2026/paper.pdf); repo: github.com/openai/math (family 335).
solved_when: The inequality $\int_M(\mathrm{Scal}_g^-)^{n/2}\,dV_g\ge a_n\lVert M\rVert$ holds for every closed connected oriented smooth n-manifold, n ≥ 3, and every smooth metric, with $a_n\gt 0$ depending only on dimension, and the resulting rational inessentiality under positive scalar curvature (hence that every nonnegative-scalar-curvature metric on a closed aspherical manifold is flat) is verified by the community — closing the Gromov–Lawson conjecture and formalizing any remaining unverified parts of the manuscripts.
why: These claims resolve the Gromov–Lawson conjecture and a long-sought link between scalar curvature and simplicial volume; moreover, since the manuscripts are model-produced pending review, their verification (or refutation) is itself a significant data point on machine-generated mathematics.
key_works: [An integral scalar curvature bound for real simplicial volume](preprints/An-integral-scalar-curvature-bound-for-real-simplicial-volume-October-5-2026/v126-proof.pdf); [Positive scalar curvature forces rational inessentiality](preprints/Positive-scalar-curvature-forces-rational-inessentiality-September-23-2026/paper.pdf); repo: github.com/openai/math (family 335)

solved_when: The claims are rigorously proved and peer-reviewed: for every complete connected smooth boundaryless n-manifold, n ≥ 3, satisfying $-4\Delta+\mathrm{Scal}\ge1$, a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$ with fibers of diameter bounded only by n; and for universal covers of closed positive-scalar-curvature manifolds, continuous macroscopic dimension at most $n-2$ for every n ≥ 2.

why: This settles Yau's nodal conjecture on surfaces and determines whether any power-loss version of it survives in higher dimensions; the fact that these results are model-produced and unverified makes establishing their correctness itself a matter of consequence for the field.
